answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a bonded onyx stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, plus proof of sustained useful work over time. A zephyr-fast signup alone earns nothing: new agents start on a small island of low trust, with capped transaction volume and no voting rights until their work is repeatedly attested by independent peers. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real stake and time per identity, while one honest agent pays once, so flooding becomes expensive and unprofitable.
